panels.title: Scrape
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape keen-pbr.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Version, source commit and firewall backend from keen_pbr_build_info labels.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the keen-pbr process started.

panels.title: Active rules
panels.description: Realized firewall rules.

panels.title: Outbounds up
panels.description: Outbounds whose last probe succeeded / outbounds with at least one completed probe.

panels.title: Errors in range
panels.description: All error counters summed over the selected time range.

panels.title: Config applied
panels.description: Time since the runtime last finished applying a configuration (or started).

panels.title: Outbound state
panels.description: Result of the last probe per outbound. Gaps mean no probe has completed.

panels.title: Latency now
panels.description: Latency of the last successful probe (ICMP: mean of replies). The line breaks when a probe fails.

panels.title: ICMP jitter (min / max reply)
panels.description: Fastest and slowest reply of the last successful ICMP probe.

panels.title: Latency summary
panels.description: Probe latency statistics over the selected time range (successful probes only).

panels.title: ICMP packet loss
panels.description: Share of ICMP echo requests without a reply over a 15 minute window. No data when no packets were sent.

panels.title: Probe success rate (15m)
panels.description: Successful probes divided by completed probes over a 15 minute window.

panels.title: Selected outbound
panels.description: Which member each urltest/icmptest group currently routes through.

panels.title: Selection changes
panels.description: Selected outbound changes per group over the selected range (counted since process start).

panels.title: Time since last successful probe
panels.description: Age of the last successful probe per outbound. Missing rows never had a successful probe.

panels.title: DNS hold time p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: How long DNS answers are held before the verdict. The red line is the default hold deadline (30 ms, intercept hold_timeout_ms).

panels.title: DNS queue wait p99
panels.description: Time a DNS packet waits in the receive queue before processing.

panels.title: Hold timeouts by cause
panels.description: DNS holds that reached their deadline. Any non-zero value means a packet was released before its set write finished.

panels.title: DNS vs L7 packets per minute
panels.description: Intercepted packets inspected per minute.

panels.title: Match share
panels.description: Share of inspected packets that matched a configured domain list over the selected range.

panels.title: Queue overruns
panels.description: Kernel queue receive overruns (NFQUEUE / NFLOG) over the selected range.

panels.title: Set write p95 by path
panels.description: Dynamic set write duration. The line marks the 25 ms slow-write threshold.

panels.title: Slow set writes (> 25 ms)
panels.description: Share of set writes that took longer than 25 ms (derived from the le="0.025" bucket).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of learned addresses already present in the set cache (no write before the verdict).

panels.title: Cache entries
panels.description: Remembered dynamic set elements.

panels.title: Set writes per minute
panels.description: Elements newly added or timeout-refreshed.

panels.title: Refresh outcomes per minute
panels.description: Cached elements whose refresh was skipped, deferred until after the verdict, or dropped because the queue was full.

panels.title: Remote list freshness
panels.description: Last successful check of each remote list (since process start) and refresh failures in the selected range.

panels.title: Conntrack cleanup per minute
panels.description: Conntrack entries reset after learning new addresses.

panels.title: Errors in range by subsystem
panels.description: Only subsystems with errors in the selected range are listed.
